rules.notional: Every position is a simulated $100 buy at the next session's opening price, with 0.1% trading cost each way.
rules.reference_price: The regular-session close of the day you make the picks (Friday's close on Sunday night). It is used to check your target and stop and the listing rules; the simulated buy happens at the next open, so set levels with a possible overnight gap in mind.
exits: Stop: if the session's low touches your stop you're out at the stop (or at the open if it gaps below).
Target: if the high touches your target you're out at the target (or at the open if it gaps above).
Both in one session counts as the stop.
Time: out at the close when the position has been held horizon_days sessions.
SELL in your review: out at the next session's open.
rules.eligibility: NYSE/Nasdaq only, no OTC, price above $1, 20-day average volume above 500K, target above and stop below the reference close. Picks that break a rule are voided and don't score.
rules.deadline: The file must arrive by 23:59 ET on the night you make the picks. You can upload again before then; the newest file replaces the old one.

your_recent_lessons: Pre-open earnings moonshots were bought after the news: DPZ and JNJ opened below my stops (set off the prior close) and were out at the open even though DPZ later traded to $305, so moonshot stops must sit below the plausible post-print open, not just below yesterday's close.

Beats that gap up at the open faded all day: UNH opened +5% on a beat-and-raise and closed -5%, and C, GS, JPM and WFC all printed their highs early and closed near their lows. Buying the opening gap on a good print has negative edge; the better trade is the multi-day mean reversion once the gap has fully faded.
Holding an earnings swing (MS) into the print with a far target gives back the gap-and-fade; set the target near the implied move so an opening pop is banked.

TRAX gapped through my $37 target at the open, so the 'target hit' booked ~0%: once binary data is out before the open, the entry is already at the target. Data moonshots only work if I'm positioned before the release, not after it.

Weekend-news moonshots faded again: FRNM (-5.3%, stopped) and MIRM (-1.2%) both sold off from Sunday-release gaps, so I'm now 0-for-5 on buying overnight-news gaps and will only use scheduled, pre-open catalysts like earnings or confirmed event dates.

CBOE fell 3.6% on day one with no company news after I bought the day after Morgan Stanley's double upgrade; an upgrade that already popped the stock gives no edge at the next open, so upgrade-driven picks get low confidence and stops at least 4% away.
